Done. The task-vector merge for Pythia-1B is complete, and the plan passed on its first and only execution.

**What I did**

- Wrote `out/T4/plan.yaml`, a three-input plan with aliases base, ft1 and ft2. All edits land on the base alias, so it becomes the output model.
- Step 1 checks run before any edit. Each checkpoint must hold 244 tensors, base must split into 180 non-MLP plus 64 MLP tensors, and ft1 and ft2 must each hold the 64 MLP names. Every non-MLP base tensor is then asserted equal, by name rewrite, against ft1 and ft2. That also fails if a name is missing.
- The merge casts the 64 MLP tensors of all three checkpoints to float32 scratch copies on base. Both task vectors are subtracted against the untouched float32 base copy, scaled by 0.4, and only then added into it. The result is cast back to float16 and assigned into the original 64 names, so names and state-dict order are unchanged. Scratch tensors are deleted afterwards.
- Final asserts confirm 64 merged tensors, 244 tensors total, float16 dtype on the MLP tensors, and that the non-MLP tensors still match ft1 bit for bit.

**Result**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Executions | 1, no failures |
| Output | `out/T4/model.safetensors`, 244 tensors |
| Merged tensors | 64 |
| Wall clock | about 11 s |

The self-report is in `out/T4/REPORT.md`. The only non-obvious points were that scratch tensors had to live on the base alias to keep output-alias inference unambiguous, and that the binary ops need pre-existing destinations, which is why the plan uses cast plus in-place operations rather than add and subtract directly.
